fullText:
Summary: CIC Holdings (CIC.N0000 voting, CIC.X0000 non-voting) is a decent, growing group, but both share classes are priced well above what its returns support. Redone with the beta-based required return now used for every company: a beta of 1.08 (provisional) gives a cost of equity of 19.3%, against the 18% set by hand before, and the P/E method now uses a justified P/E instead of the market's 8x. Returns on equity of 15–16% are below that 19.3%, so the methods put fair value at about Rs 16.60 (0.65x NAV of Rs 25.52), down from Rs 22.60. At Rs 28.80 the voting share is about 73% above it; the non-voting share at Rs 25.00, with the same dividends and earnings, is 13% cheaper but still about 50% above. I'd buy at up to about Rs 14.10 and treat under Rs 12.50 as a strong buy. Still a 'good' business (3 of 4 tests): watch list.

Price and key figures
Price: voting Rs 28.80 and non-voting Rs 25.00 (CSE closing price, 13 November 2026). Please check them live. In April–September 2026 the voting share traded between Rs 27.00 and Rs 32.00, and it closed the year to March 2026 at Rs 29.90. All per-share figures are after the 1-for-5 share split of October 2025.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (group, unaudited): revenue rose 3% to Rs 42.9bn and profit attributable to shareholders rose 22% to Rs 3.17bn. EPS was Rs 1.67 against Rs 1.37, so trailing 12-month EPS is Rs 3.94.
What drove it: livestock solutions (results up 31%), industrial solutions (up 47%) and health and personal care (up 10%) grew, while agri solutions fell (revenue down 12%, results down 27%). The share of associates' profit, mainly John Keells, rose to Rs 673mn from Rs 275mn. Net finance costs rose 26% to Rs 1.33bn.
Year to March 2026 (group): revenue Rs 91.8bn (up 10%), profit attributable Rs 6.91bn (up 27%), EPS Rs 3.64 (Rs 2.87), ROE 15%, NAV Rs 24.37, dividend Rs 0.50 (14% of profit). Debt Rs 30.2bn, 56% of equity; Rs 35.0bn at September 2026.
John Keells: CIC equity-accounts its effective holding of about 6% of John Keells Holdings. Its share of JKH's net assets was Rs 33.4bn at 30 June 2026, about Rs 17.60 of CIC's Rs 25.52 NAV per share, carried at book value, not JKH's market price.

What changed in this redo
The required return now comes from the beta, as for every company. Beta 1.08 (provisional) gives a cost of equity of 19.3% (bear 20.8%, bull 17.8%), against 18% (20% / 16.5%) set by hand before. The P/E method now uses the justified P/E (about 4.5x forward in the base case) instead of the 6 / 8 / 10x the market has paid, because at ROE below the required return the market's multiple implies more value than CIC's returns support. Business tests unchanged (3 of 4); category unchanged (watch list).

Required return
Cost of equity = risk-free 8.24% (12.24% 10-year bond less 4.0% default spread) + beta 1.08 × (mature premium 4.2% + country premium 6.08%) = 19.3%.
Beta, step by step: CIC has four operating segments (agri, livestock, industrial, health and personal care) and a John Keells stake. With no segment profit split in the record, I averaged Damodaran's global unlevered, cash-corrected betas for Farming/Agriculture 0.49, Food Processing 0.56, Chemical (Diversified) 0.91 and Drugs (Pharmaceutical) 1.00: 0.74. His emerging-markets file couldn't be opened in this run, so these are web-search extracts and not all are confirmed as January 2026. Relevered with gross borrowings of Rs 35.0bn against a market value of Rs 52.9bn (cash isn't in the record, so this overstates debt a little) at 30% tax: 1.08. No local 5-year beta was found (Simply Wall St 0.19 with no period; TradingView's 1.32 is a 1-year figure). It's provisional; refresh in January 2027.
WACC isn't worked out: interest paid and cash aren't in the record, and no DCF is used.

Methods
NAV (Rs 25.52): voting 1.13x, non-voting 0.98x.
Return on equity: 15% for the year to March 2026 and about 16% over the last 12 months; 14% in the year to March 2025.
P/E: 7.3x trailing EPS of Rs 3.94 (voting), 6.3x (non-voting). Year-end P/E (voting): 8.2x (2026), 8.2x (2025), 2.7x (2024), 3.5x (2023), 3.9x (2022).
Dividends: Rs 0.50 a year, a 1.7% yield (2.0% non-voting), about 14% of profit.
Justified price to book: (ROE − g) ÷ (r − g) = 0.51x / 0.68x / 0.93x NAV: Rs 12.9 / 17.3 / 23.6, weighted Rs 17.2.
P/E method: EPS to March 2027 of Rs 3.60 / 4.20 / 4.50 × justified P/E 3.9x / 4.5x / 5.4x: Rs 14.0 / 18.9 / 24.5, weighted Rs 18.5. The base EPS is 6.6% above the Rs 3.94 run-rate.
Residual income: Rs 8.2 / 14.2 / 22.6, weighted Rs 14.1.
Dividend model: Rs 3.3 / 4.0 / 5.0 (not used in the fair value).

Growth check: the residual income paths imply earnings growth of about 9.6% / 12.6% / 14.5% a year over the next five years. CIC keeps 86% of its profit and earns 15% on equity, which supports 12.9%, so all three are within 2 points. Long-run growth of 5–7% stays below the 12.24% bond yield and needs about 40% of profit reinvested at a 15% ROE. A capex-based check isn't possible: capex and depreciation aren't in the record.
CIC keeps about 86% of its profit, so a dividend model badly understates it. A whole-company DCF isn't used: much of profit is its share of John Keells, which isn't paid in cash, and the record has no capex, depreciation, cash or interest paid (a /redo CIC full would add them). All three methods value CIC below book because ROE of 15–16% is under the 19.3% required return.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity: 20.8% / 19.3% / 17.8%.
Long-run ROE (price to book): 13% / 15% / 17%.
ROE path (residual income): 15% falling to 12% / 16% falling to 15% / 17% held; payout 15%.
Long-term growth: 5% / 6% / 7%.
EPS for the year to March 2027 × justified P/E: 3.60 × 3.9 / 4.20 × 4.5 / 4.50 × 5.4.
Average of the three methods: Rs 11.7 / Rs 16.8 / Rs 23.6.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives about Rs 16.60 (0.65x NAV), down from Rs 22.60. The voting share at Rs 28.80 is about 73% above it; the non-voting share at Rs 25.00 is about 50% above it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 14.10, and 25% gives Rs 12.50. The same levels apply to the non-voting share, which has the same economic rights; it's the cheaper way in.
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 16.50, 150 at up to Rs 14.10 and 150 at up to Rs 12.50. That averages about Rs 14.58, about Rs 7,290, against Rs 12,500 for non-voting shares at Rs 25.00.
Realism: not realistic soon. The non-voting share would need to fall about 34% to reach the first tier and 44% to reach the buy price; the voting share's low in April–September 2026 was Rs 27.00. It would take a broad market fall, or lower interest rates cutting the required return.

Sensitivity (residual income base case, Rs per share)
Cost of equity 17.8%: 11.6 / 17.3 / 24.2 for long-run ROE of 12% / 15% / 18%.
Cost of equity 19.3%: 9.6 / 14.2 / 19.7.
Cost of equity 20.8%: 8.2 / 11.9 / 16.3.
On book value, today's voting price needs a cost of equity of about 16% and a long-run ROE of about 17%, which would need a beta near 0.75.

Business tests (3 of 4, good)
Return on equity 15%: pass, only just. Debt 0.56x equity: pass. Steady profit: pass, though uneven (EPS Rs 1.94 to Rs 5.14 over five years). Profit into cash and dividends: fail (14% paid out; part of profit is the John Keells share). Category unchanged: watch list.

What would change my view
Supports a higher value: agri solutions recovering; livestock, industrial and health growth continuing; John Keells' profits rising; a higher dividend payout; lower interest rates or a lower beta (each point off the cost of equity adds roughly Rs 2); fuller figures from a /redo CIC full.
Supports a lower value: rising debt and finance costs; weather, fertiliser prices or policy changes hurting agri solutions; John Keells' share price staying below the book value CIC carries it at; a weaker rupee raising imported raw material costs; the controlling shareholder's interests differing from minority shareholders'.

These are my estimates from the research record, redone on 15 November 2026. The interim figures are unaudited and the beta is provisional, so check the price before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
